profile: Share of revenue from work at customers’ premises (%)
All workers hold the registrations, licences or certificates their work needs?

gen: Registrations and licences
Check every worker holds the licence or registration their work requires, and that it is current. Lapsed licences can affect cover and create regulatory exposure.
liab: Subcontractors and labour hire
Do they hold their own insurance, written indemnities and the right licences? Ask who is responsible for their safety and their defective work.
Damage to customers’ property
Water, fire and impact damage on customer sites are the usual claims. Check the excess and any exclusions that apply to the work being done.
statutory: Hazard identification, site induction, contractor management and incident recording. Officers have due diligence duties under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.

liab: Work at height
Ladders, scaffolds, roofs and elevated work platforms. Ask about fall protection, operator competence and edge protection, and falls onto people or property below.

mdamage: Hot work done (welding, grinding, soldering, brazing, cutting)?
Hot work permit and fire watch procedure used?
Welding, grinding and cutting cause fires, often after the crew has left. Ask about permits, fire watch, extinguishers and flammable storage.
Is stock insured at the peak value, not the average? Include stock held offsite, in transit and on consignment, and check theft and spoilage limits.

machinery: Which single machine, if it failed, would stop trading? Ask about service contracts, spare parts and replacement lead times.

profile: Share of products imported or sourced from overseas suppliers (%)

liab: Product liability and recall

Faulty or unsafe products, labelling errors and recalls. Importers and distributors carry the manufacturer’s liability if the manufacturer cannot be pursued. Check supplier contracts and recall cover.
Exports and overseas jurisdiction
Sales to the USA and Canada raise liability limits and legal costs. Ask where products or services end up, and check the territorial and jurisdiction wording.

profile: Food Act 2014 food control plan or national programme in place?
Allergen controls and staff training recorded?
Cold chain monitored with alarms or logs?

gen: Food safety registration
Confirm the food control plan or national programme, the verifier and the last verification result. Non-compliance can close a premises.
liab: Food poisoning and allergens
Check the policy covers food poisoning and allergic reactions, and whether product recall or contamination cover is needed.
mdamage: Loss of chilled and frozen stock from equipment breakdown or power failure. Check the limit, the alarm conditions and the excess.
Deep fryers or open flame cooking?
Kitchen extract and canopy cleaned regularly?
Fryers, canopies and grease build-up cause the biggest hospitality fires. Ask about extract cleaning frequency, suppression systems, extinguishers and the evacuation scheme.

profile: Licence breaches, infringements or committee hearings in the last 3 years?

gen: Licence and compliance

Licence type, hours and conditions, duty manager certificates and the host responsibility policy. Ask about District Licensing Committee or police contact. A suspension is a business interruption event.
liab: Alcohol-related incidents
Assaults, intoxication and glass injuries. ACC covers injury in NZ, so check what is exposed: defence costs, property damage and exemplary damages.
statutory: Sale and Supply of Alcohol Act, Food Act and health and safety matters. Check defence cost cover. Fines under health and safety law cannot be insured.

profile: Police vetting and safety checks on all staff and volunteers?
Written child protection policy in place?

gen: Children’s safety checking
Safety checks on staff and volunteers, supervision rules and a code of conduct. The Children’s Act 2014 requires safety checking for some children’s workers.
liab: Abuse and molestation
Check whether it is covered, the limit, and whether defence costs are included. Many general liability policies exclude it. Confirm this first.

profile: Number of clients or residents in care
Complaints, incidents or audits with adverse findings in the last 3 years?
Staff safety checked and training records current?

gen: Standards and audits
Certification and audit results, complaints, restraint and medication management, and incident reporting. Adverse audit findings affect underwriting.
liab: Abuse, neglect and care claims
Check abuse and neglect cover, defence costs, and professional liability for care decisions. Ask about historical claims and complaints to oversight bodies.

profile: All practitioners hold current practising certificates?
Complaints or notifications to regulators or the Health and Disability Commissioner in the last 5 years?
Patient records held electronically with backups?

gen: Registration and scope
Practising certificates, scope of practice and indemnity requirements of the registration body. Check locums and contractors are covered.
Complaints and claims history
Complaints to the Health and Disability Commissioner or professional body. Any circumstances that could become a claim must be notified to the current insurer.
pi: Check continuous cover, retroactive date, run-off cover for retiring practitioners, and cover for locums, students and non-clinical advice.

profile: Largest single fee or project value

gen: Scope of services
Exactly what is advised or delivered, and what has changed. New services outside the proposal can fall outside cover.
pi: Claims-made cover depends on continuity and the retroactive date. Notify circumstances before the policy ends. Check run-off if the business changes or closes.
Who drafts the terms? Limitation of liability, caps, warranties of outcome and indemnities in customer contracts.
Work for clients in the USA or Canada, and the policy’s territory and jurisdiction wording.

cyber: What personal information is held, where it sits and who can access it. A breach brings notification duties under the Privacy Act 2020.
Backups tested, offline or immutable copies, and how long the business could operate without its systems.
crime: Fake invoices and changed bank details are the most common loss. Check dual authorisation and callback verification.

fleet: Tools or stock regularly carried in vehicles?
Driver ages, licences and driving records, tracking devices, and whether vehicles are used privately. Check tools and stock carried in vehicles.

crime: Cash on site, banking routine, till variances and access to the safe. Check employee dishonesty cover and limits.
Compare the highest amounts with the policy limits for each situation: in hours, in a safe out of hours, in transit and at someone’s home. Peak days and long weekends are when limits are breached.
Safe, keys and who can open it
Rated and anchored safe, who holds codes, dual control, and whether codes change when staff leave. Insurers often attach safe conditions to higher money limits.
Who banks, how often, how much at a time, and whether routes and times vary. Large cash holdings are usually better handled by a cash-in-transit contractor or a smart safe.
Cash that cannot be banked over a long weekend builds up. Check the out-of-hours limit and the safe rating for those peaks.

High-theft stock such as electronics, tobacco or alcohol?

gen: Shopfront and security
Ram raids and burglary. Ask about roller doors, bollards, cameras, alarm monitoring and smoke or fog devices.
liab: Customer injury on premises
Slips, trips and falling stock. Check wet-weather matting, cleaning logs and incident records.
bi: Stock and income peaks before Christmas or other seasons. Sums insured and indemnity periods should reflect the peak.

profile: Quad bikes, side-by-sides or tractors in use?
Agrichemicals stored and applied under a certified handler?
Irrigation, effluent or water consents held?

gen: Farm structure and ownership
Trust, company or partnership, who owns the land and who owns the stock, plant and improvements. Make sure the right interests are noted.
Seasonal peaks
Stock numbers, crop values and plant use peak in season. Sums insured should reflect the peak.
liab: Farm liability
Visitors, contractors, spray drift, stock on roads, fires lit on the farm and farm park or tourism activities.
Biosecurity and pollution
Biosecurity breaches, effluent discharge and chemical spills. Check pollution cover and consent conditions.
statutory: Quad bikes, tractors, chemicals and young or casual workers. Fines under health and safety law cannot be insured, but defence costs can.
mdamage: Sheds, dairy shed, fences, effluent systems and irrigation. Ask about the age and condition of plant and the replacement values.
Theft of tools from vehicles and sites is the main property loss. Check the limit per vehicle and any locked-storage conditions.

cworks.name: Contract Works
cworks.desc: Projects under construction, plant and materials on site
q: Total value of contracts started in the year
Work on or beside existing structures?
Excavation, piling or work near boundaries?
Weather protection used on open structures?

cworks: Contract value including owner-supplied materials, the maintenance period and cover for existing structures worked on.
Water damage during construction is a leading loss. Ask about temporary protection and weathertightness controls.
Tools and materials on site. Fencing, lockable storage and overnight security.
Excavation, vibration and removal of support. Check adjoining property cover and exclusions.

Who is responsible for cash in the machines and machine damage?

crime: Machine break-ins or robberies in the last 5 years?
TAB or betting terminals on site?
Gaming machines and who carries the cash risk

Class 4 machines are run by gaming societies. The venue agreement decides who is responsible for cash in the machines and for machine damage. Confirm what the society insures and what the venue must cover.
Gaming room cash and money limits
Notes held in machines, payout cash and tickets awaiting redemption. Check the highest holding against the money limit and the safe or room security.
Gaming rooms are a target for burglary. Ask about forced entry history, alarm response and CCTV.

docs: Venue agreement with the gaming society
Latest gaming machine cash collection record

Highest balance held at any time

External review or audit of the accounts

crime: Bank details changes verified by phone call to a known number?
Payment fraud or email-compromise attempts in the last 3 years?
Client money and the policy limit
Compare the peak balance with the crime and fidelity limit. A settlement day can hold many times the usual balance.
Dual authorisation, limits per approver, and bank details changes verified by call-back. Email-compromise fraud is the common loss.
Trust account duties depend on the profession (lawyers, conveyancers, real estate agents, accountants, financial advice). Check what the regulator requires and what cover the rules expect.

opts: Mineral wool or other fire-rated core

mdamage: Share of the building that is panelled
Fire rating certificate held for the panels? (FR grade datasheet, FM or LPCB approval)
Heat sources, hot work or cooking equipment fixed to or near the panels?

Foam-core panels can spread fire quickly and many insurers load, restrict or decline cover. Ask for the core type, how much of the building is panelled, the fire rating certificate, and whether coolrooms, cooking or hot work sit next to them.

profile: Defective workmanship / PBWO extension wanted on the liability policy?
Contracts require PBWO or defects cover?
Claims or complaints about faulty work or rework in the last 5 years?
Details of those claims or complaints

liab: Defective workmanship and PBWO: ask for it by name

Standard liability wordings usually exclude (1) the cost of redoing the insured's own faulty work and (2) damage to the property being worked on (PBWO), which is where many trade claims sit. Ask for the Defective Workmanship / PBWO extension to be quoted as a separate option with its own limit and excess, rather than assuming it is included.
Where to get it: market approach for trades

Small-business and tradie package policies often exclude PBWO or cap it at a low sub-limit. Contractors' liability underwriters and specialist or wholesale facilities are more likely to offer it, usually with a higher excess, a sub-limit and conditions. Get at least two quotes with the extension priced separately and compare the wording, not just the limit.
Read the wording behind the extension

Check what is bought back: damage to PBWO caused by faulty work is the aim, while rectifying the defect itself usually stays excluded. Compare sub-limit and aggregate, excess, claims-made or retro date, completed-works period, subcontractors' work, and exclusions for weathertightness, waterproofing, structural work and hot works.
Match the contract requirements
Head contractors and principals often require PBWO or defects cover. Check the contract wording and make sure the certificate of currency shows the extension and the limit.
